God Equation Path B — Family A: Channel Intensity Observables (2026-04-01)

Bounded theorem attempt and kill test for closure-time channel intensities as H_prod observables

Status: CANDIDATE RESTRICTED NO-GO — theorem attempt shows failure for the direct local raw-intensity branch under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble, not a universal Family A kill Assigned: Claude (derivation) → Codex (audit) Do not promote without Codex sign-off. Truth sources: god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md, god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md, z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md *** ## 0. Setup

We follow the minimal work program in Section 7 of the observable spec.

One admissible observable family only: Family A — closure-time channel intensities.

Observable definition:

X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|²   for r ∈ {0, 1, 2}

where t₃ is the 3-step closure time and χ_r(t₃) is the field amplitude in channel r at closure.

System: one ℤ₃ medium with three coupled channels. Linearized EOM:

(□ + m²) δχ_j = κ(δχ_{j−1} + δχ_{j+1}) + (λ/3) δT

1. Admissibility Check

Test A — One-system support ✓

All three observables are defined on the same medium at the same closure time.

Test B — Non-one-hot support ✓

The intensities |χ_r|² are continuous-valued. A field configuration can carry simultaneous amplitude in all three channels. The relation X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = const is not forced by definition (it would require Σ|χ_r|² = const, which is an energy constraint, not an automatic identity).

Test C — Physical readout ✓

Channel amplitudes χ_r are the actual field variables of the ℤ₃ Lagrangian.

Test D — Actual-operator dependence ✓

The closure uses the actual κ-coupled dynamics, not the pure-shift shortcut.

Test E — Independence strength ✓ (target only)

Full joint-law factorization is the target. Covariance-level decoupling is not accepted as closure.

Family A passes all five admissibility tests. Proceed to factorization analysis. *** ## 2. Randomness Source and Probability Space

For Family A to yield a non-trivial probability distribution (not just deterministic numbers), we need a source of randomness. Two physically motivated choices:

Choice I — Initial field fluctuations (ensemble over initial conditions)

Take the initial field configuration χ(0) = (χ₀(0), χ₁(0), χ₂(0)) drawn from a Gaussian ensemble with isotropic covariance:

E[χ_i(0) χ_j(0)] = σ² δ_{ij}
E[χ_i(0)] = 0

This represents thermal fluctuations or vacuum fluctuations in the initial state.

Choice II — Vacuum state of the quantum field theory

In the free linearized theory, the vacuum state is a Gaussian state with covariance:

C_{ij} = ⟨χ_i χ_j⟩ = (1/3) Σ_k σ_k² e^{2πik(i−j)/3}

where σ_k² = ⟨|χ̃_k|²⟩ is the zero-point fluctuation amplitude for normal mode k.

Both choices lead to the same structure. We work with Choice I (initial fluctuation ensemble) as the simpler case. *** ## 3. The Closure Map

Under the linearized EOM (dropping the source term δT for the pure propagation analysis), the 3-step closure map is:

χ(t₃) = T_sym³ · χ(0)

where T_sym³ = (1/4)I + (3/8)S̄ + (3/8)S̄².

Explicitly:

T_sym³ = [ 1/4   3/8   3/8 ]
          [ 3/8   1/4   3/8 ]
          [ 3/8   3/8   1/4 ]

This is a doubly stochastic matrix. Row sums and column sums are all 1. *** ## 4. Joint Distribution of Channel Intensities

Under the initial-fluctuation ensemble (Choice I), the output field at closure is:

χ_r(t₃) = Σ_s [T_sym³]_{rs} χ_s(0) = (1/4)χ_r(0) + (3/8)χ_{r−1}(0) + (3/8)χ_{r+1}(0)

(indices mod 3).

The intensity observables are:

X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|² = |(1/4)χ_r(0) + (3/8)χ_{r−1}(0) + (3/8)χ_{r+1}(0)|²

4.1 Means and Variances

For real fields with E[χ_i(0) χ_j(0)] = σ² δ_{ij}:

E[X^(r)] = E[|χ_r(t₃)|²]
          = [(1/4)² + (3/8)² + (3/8)²] σ²
          = [1/16 + 9/64 + 9/64] σ²
          = [4/64 + 9/64 + 9/64] σ²
          = (22/64) σ²
          = (11/32) σ²

All three channels have the same expected intensity, as required by ℤ₃ symmetry.

4.2 Cross-Covariance — Critical Computation

Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) = E[X^(0) X^(1)] − E[X^(0)] E[X^(1)]

For zero-mean Gaussian variables, by Isserlis’ theorem (Wick’s theorem):

E[X^(0) X^(1)] = E[|χ_0(t₃)|² |χ_1(t₃)|²]
               = E[χ_0(t₃)² χ_1(t₃)²]   (real fields)
               = 2[E[χ_0(t₃) χ_1(t₃)]]² + E[χ_0(t₃)²] E[χ_1(t₃)²]

The cross-correlation:

E[χ_0(t₃) χ_1(t₃)] = Σ_{s,u} [T_sym³]_{0s} [T_sym³]_{1u} E[χ_s(0) χ_u(0)]
                     = σ² Σ_s [T_sym³]_{0s} [T_sym³]_{1s}
                     = σ² [(1/4)(3/8) + (3/8)(1/4) + (3/8)(3/8)]
                     = σ² [3/32 + 3/32 + 9/64]
                     = σ² [6/64 + 6/64 + 9/64]
                     = (21/64) σ²

Therefore:

E[X^(0) X^(1)] = 2[(21/64) σ²]² + [(11/32) σ²]²
               = (882/4096) σ⁴ + (121/1024) σ⁴
               = (882/4096) σ⁴ + (484/4096) σ⁴
               = (1366/4096) σ⁴
E[X^(0)] E[X^(1)] = [(11/32) σ²]² = (121/1024) σ⁴ = (484/4096) σ⁴
Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) = (1366/4096) σ⁴ − (484/4096) σ⁴ = (882/4096) σ⁴ = (441/2048) σ⁴ > 0

5. Main Finding

The direct local raw-intensity branch of Family A does NOT factorize under the κ-coupled closure dynamics for the isotropic Gaussian ensemble.

The cross-covariance is:

Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) = (441/2048) σ⁴ = 2[(21/64) σ²]² > 0

The joint law P(X^(0), X^(1), X^(2)) is not a product of marginals for this ensemble. The observables are positively correlated. The baseline direct raw-intensity route fails here.

Why the correlation is nonzero

The correlation source is transparent:

E[χ_0(t₃) χ_1(t₃)] = σ² Σ_s [T_sym³]_{0s} [T_sym³]_{1s} = (21/64) σ² ≠ 0

because T_sym³ has non-zero off-diagonal entries (3/8 throughout). Two output channels share input from the same initial channel (e.g., both χ_0(t₃) and χ_1(t₃) receive amplitude from χ_1(0) with coefficients 3/8 and 1/4 respectively), creating unavoidable correlation.

Structural root cause

The off-diagonal entries of T_sym³ are larger than the diagonal (3/8 > 1/4). This is the same finding as Q-D in the route audit: the κ coupling produces off-diagonal terms that are not subleading at the 3-step closure scale. The intensity correlations directly inherit this structure. *** ## 6. Does the κ→0 Limit Help?

In the limit κ → 0, the three channels decouple. Then T_sym → (1/2)S̄ + (1/2)S̄²… wait, that is still symmetric.

More carefully: for a purely diagonal (no κ coupling) medium, T would be diagonal and T³ = I (identity). Then χ_r(t₃) = χ_r(0) and the intensities are X^(r) = |χ_r(0)|², which ARE independent under the isotropic ensemble. So at κ = 0, Family A factorizes.

For the actual ℤ₃ nearest-neighbor EOM:

T = (1/2)(S̄ + S̄²)   (κ = 1/2 in normalized units)
T_sym³ diagonal entries = 1/4,  off-diagonal = 3/8

The off-diagonal entries are larger than the diagonal. Family A fails at the actual coupling strength by a large margin, not as a small perturbative effect. *** ## 7. Can a Different Readout Map Save Family A?

The covariance analysis above uses X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|² as a direct intensity readout. Could a different function F_r(|χ_0|², |χ_1|², |χ_2|²) factorize?

For the direct raw-intensity readout X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|², positive covariance is proved.

For more general channel-local transforms F_r(|χ_r(t₃)|²), this file does not prove a full no-go. It only shows that the baseline Family A readout already fails under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble.

For a function that depends on all three channels (F_r depends on all |χ_s|²), the observable is no longer a simple channel-local intensity and may be drifting toward a different family. *** ## 8. Verdict

Direct Family A raw intensities are a strong restricted no-go candidate under the actual κ-coupled closure dynamics and the isotropic Gaussian input ensemble.

Test Result
Admissibility (5 tests) PASS
Factorization under isotropic ensemble FAIL: Cov(X(0),X(1)) = (441/2048)σ⁴ > 0
κ→0 limit PASS (decoupled case is fine, but unphysical)
Alternative readout maps Still open beyond the direct raw-intensity readout

The correlation is not a small perturbative effect. The off-diagonal entries of T_sym³ (3/8) exceed the diagonal (1/4). Any probability model using simultaneous channel intensities on the actual ℤ₃ closure object inherits positive correlation between channels.

Pending Codex verification: this kill argument should be reviewed for:

  1. Whether the isotropic Gaussian ensemble for χ(0) is the physically correct choice, or whether a different (non-isotropic, non-Gaussian) input ensemble could produce factorization
  2. Whether the Isserlis/Wick computation is correct for the specific Gaussian model used
  3. Whether any broader channel-intensity readout beyond direct raw intensities survives without changing families

If Codex confirms all three checks: the direct raw-intensity branch of Family A is dead. Broader Family A variants would still need separate elimination. *** ## 9. Implication for the Broader Path B Program

If the direct raw-intensity branch of Family A is killed:

  • The simultaneous-channel-intensity approach fails because the closure operator itself is too correlated at the 3-step scale
  • Family B (integrated channel currents) faces the same off-diagonal problem unless the time-integrated current suppresses the κ-generated correlations (requires explicit computation)
  • Family C (quadratic closure functionals of the actual operator) is the most abstract remaining route; it may allow construction of uncorrelated observables by design, but the physical justification then becomes the main obstacle

The root difficulty is structural: the ℤ₃ nearest-neighbor coupling makes the 3-step closure operator highly non-diagonal. Any observable that directly reads out channel-specific information at closure will be correlated, because multiple output channels share the same input channels through the coupling.

The only escape would be a physical reason why only one output channel carries information after closure (i.e., selection to one channel — which is the one-hot picture already killed) or a non-trivial decoupling mechanism not visible in the current operator. ** Draft: Claude Code (2026-04-01). Awaiting Codex audit before any confidence update.*

God Equation Path B — Family B: Integrated Channel Currents (2026-04-01)

Bounded theorem attempt and kill test for time-integrated channel observables as H_prod candidates

Status: RESTRICTED NO-GO CANDIDATE — the two tested quadratic time-integrated readouts fail strongly under the isotropic Gaussian probe; later Codex audit/extension showed the Family A whitening covariance does not rescue B1/B2, and the remaining edge-flux current must be treated separately Author: Claude Code (2026-04-01) Assigned: Claude (derivation) → Codex (audit) Do not promote without Codex sign-off. Truth sources: - god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md (admissibility tests) - god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_theorem_2026-04-01.md (Family A restricted no-go) - god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md (Codex audit — covariance formula) - z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md (ℤ₃ Lagrangian and EOM) - god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md (route audit, structural constraints) - god_eq_path_b_edge_flux_current_no_go_2026-04-01.md (later exact no-go for the remaining natural current-style observable)

Addendum (later 2026-04-01): - the exact B1 covariance is 7729/2048 sigma^4, stronger than the lower bound proved below - the Family A whitening covariance is not a shared escape hatch for B1/B2 - the antisymmetric edge-flux current is handled separately and does not survive either *** ## 0. Why Family B Exists

Family A (closure-time channel intensities X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|²) is a restricted no-go under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble, but not a universal kill. The Family A audit named three surviving escape routes:

  1. Specially correlated initial ensemble (the C₃-invariant Σ = A^{-2} escape hatch)
  2. Broader intensity-style readouts beyond direct local intensities
  3. Non-quadratic readouts

Family B tests route (2): can time integration of the channel dynamics suppress the cross-channel correlations that killed the point-in-time Family A readout?

Physical motivation: the ℤ₃ Lagrangian inter-channel coupling −κ Σⱼ χⱼ χⱼ₊₁ generates inter-channel currents. The integrated current over the full closure captures the total exchange between channels, not just the snapshot at t₃. If the time integration accumulates enough cancellation between early and late-time contributions, the channel observables could decouple.

For the two quadratic readouts treated in this file, the answer is: it does not. *** ## 1. Setup — The Two Family B Candidates

The ℤ₃ linearized EOM under the κ-coupled dynamics gives the step-by-step map:

χ(tₙ) = T_sym · χ(tₙ₋₁),   T_sym = (1/2)(S̄ + S̄²)

The 3-step closure operator is:

T_sym³ = (1/4)I + (3/8)S̄ + (3/8)S̄²

explicitly:

T_sym³ = [ 1/4   3/8   3/8 ]
          [ 3/8   1/4   3/8 ]
          [ 3/8   3/8   1/4 ]

Family B defines two natural integrated observables:

Candidate B1 — Integrated Channel Intensity (occupation time)

Y^(r) = Σ_{n=0}^{3} |χ_r(tₙ)|²

This is the total “occupation” of channel r across all closure steps. It sums the field intensity in channel r at each time step from start to closure.

Candidate B2 — Squared Net Amplitude Change

W^(r) = (χ_r(t₃) − χ_r(0))²

This is the squared net change in field amplitude in channel r from initial to closure. It captures the total exchange: how much channel r gained or lost across the full closure.

Both pass all five admissibility tests from the spec (one-system support, non-one-hot support, physical readout, actual-operator dependence, independence-strength target). *** ## 2. The General Quadratic Structure

The key observation is that both B1 and B2 are quadratic in the initial field χ(0).

For centered Gaussian input with isotropic covariance E[χᵢ(0)χⱼ(0)] = σ²δᵢⱼ, the covariance of any two quadratic observables Q_r = χ(0)ᵀ Aᵣ χ(0) (with symmetric Aᵣ) is:

Cov(Q₀, Q₁) = 2σ⁴ Tr(A₀ A₁)

This follows from the Isserlis / Wick theorem (the same formula used in the Family A audit, now applied generally).

The factorization condition Cov(Q₀, Q₁) = 0 reduces to Tr(A₀ A₁) = 0.

For any observable derived from the channel-specific closure dynamics, A₀ and A₁ are related by C₃ rotation: A₁ = R A₀ Rᵀ where R is the cyclic permutation. For these matrices to be orthogonal in the sense Tr(A₀ A₁) = 0 requires specific cancellation in the row structure of the closure operator — cancellation that T_sym³ does not provide.

The main theorem is that for all natural Family B readouts, Tr(A₀ A₁) > 0. *** ## 3. Candidate B1 — Integrated Intensity

3.1 Matrix decomposition

Y^(r) = Σ_{n=0}^{3} |χ_r(tₙ)|² = Σ_{n=0}^{3} χ(0)ᵀ (Tⁿ)ᵀ eᵣ eᵣᵀ Tⁿ χ(0)
       = χ(0)ᵀ Bᵣ χ(0)

where Bᵣ = Σ_{n=0}^{3} (Tⁿ)ᵀ eᵣ eᵣᵀ Tⁿ and eᵣ is the r-th standard basis vector.

The matrix Bᵣ accumulates the contribution of each time step. For rows aₙ^(r) = row r of T_sym^n:

Bᵣ = Σ_{n=0}^{3} (aₙ^(r))ᵀ aₙ^(r)   [sum of rank-1 outer products]

3.2 Cross-covariance

Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) = 2σ⁴ Tr(B₀ B₁)
                  = 2σ⁴ Σ_{n,m} Tr[(a_n^(0))ᵀ a_n^(0) · (a_m^(1))ᵀ a_m^(1)]
                  = 2σ⁴ Σ_{n,m} (a_n^(0) · a_m^(1))²

Each term (aₙ^(0) · a_m^(1))² is a squared dot product of rows — nonnegative. The sum is strictly positive as long as any pair of rows is non-orthogonal.

3.3 Explicit computation

The rows of T_sym^n for n = 0, 1, 2, 3:

n Row 0 of Tⁿ Row 1 of Tⁿ
0 [1, 0, 0] [0, 1, 0]
1 [0, 1/2, 1/2] [1/2, 0, 1/2]
2 [1/2, 1/4, 1/4] [1/4, 1/2, 1/4]
3 [1/4, 3/8, 3/8] [3/8, 1/4, 3/8]

Cross dot products aₙ^(0) · a_m^(1):

n 0 1 2 3
0 0 0 1/4 3/8
1 1/2 1/4 1/4 3/16
2 0 1/4 5/16 19/64
3 3/8 3/16 19/64 21/64

Squared and summed (each entry squared, all summed):

Tr(B₀ B₁) = 0 + 0 + 1/16 + 9/64
           + 1/4 + 1/16 + 1/16 + 9/256
           + 0 + 1/16 + 25/256 + 361/4096
           + 9/64 + 9/256 + 361/4096 + 441/4096

Rather than expanding all 16 terms, the key observation is that: - The n=m=3 term alone contributes (21/64)² = 441/4096 - The n=3, m=0 term contributes (3/8)² = 9/64 = 576/4096 - The n=0, m=3 term contributes (3/8)² = 576/4096 - All remaining terms are nonnegative

Lower bound:

Tr(B₀ B₁) ≥ (3/8)² + (3/8)² + (21/64)² = 576/4096 + 576/4096 + 441/4096
           = 1593/4096

Therefore:

Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) ≥ 2σ⁴ · 1593/4096 = 3186/4096 σ⁴ ≈ 0.778 σ⁴

This is more than twice as large as the Family A covariance (441/2048 σ⁴ ≈ 0.215 σ⁴). Time integration makes the correlation worse, not better.

Root cause: the initial step (n=0) has zero cross-correlation between channels (isotropic start). But every subsequent step adds positive contributions. The cross-time terms n ≠ m are also positive because the rows of T_sym^n for n ≥ 1 are all non-orthogonal to rows of T_sym^m for channels 0 and 1. Summation accumulates positive correlation; it does not cancel it. *** ## 4. Candidate B2 — Squared Net Amplitude Change

4.1 Observable and matrix

The net change in channel r over the full closure:

Δᵣ = χᵣ(t₃) − χᵣ(0) = Σⱼ [(T_sym³)ᵣⱼ − δᵣⱼ] χⱼ(0) = dᵣ · χ(0)

where dᵣ = row r of (T_sym³ − I):

d₀ = [1/4 − 1,  3/8,    3/8  ] = [−3/4,   3/8,   3/8 ]
d₁ = [3/8,     1/4 − 1, 3/8  ] = [ 3/8,  −3/4,   3/8 ]
d₂ = [3/8,      3/8,   1/4−1 ] = [ 3/8,   3/8,  −3/4 ]

The observable: W^(r) = Δᵣ² = χ(0)ᵀ Cᵣ χ(0) where Cᵣ = dᵣᵀ dᵣ.

4.2 Cross-dot-product of difference rows

d₀ · d₁ = (−3/4)(3/8) + (3/8)(−3/4) + (3/8)(3/8)
         = −9/32 − 9/32 + 9/64
         = −18/64 − 18/64 + 9/64
         = −27/64

The amplitude changes are negatively correlated: when channel 0 gains, channel 1 tends to lose. This is the physically expected “conservation-like” response to coupling.

4.3 Covariance of the squared observable

By Isserlis:

Cov(W^(0), W^(1)) = 2σ⁴ Tr(C₀ C₁) = 2σ⁴ (d₀ · d₁)²
                  = 2σ⁴ (27/64)² = 2σ⁴ · 729/4096 = 1458/4096 σ⁴ = 729/2048 σ⁴

The squared net current is positively correlated.

Cov(W^(0), W^(1)) = 729/2048 σ⁴ ≈ 0.356 σ⁴ > 0

This is larger than the Family A covariance (441/2048 σ⁴ ≈ 0.215 σ⁴).

4.4 Why squaring reverses the sign

The amplitude changes Δ₀, Δ₁ are negatively correlated (they anti-correlate because coupling is conservative: if one channel gains, neighbors tend to lose). But the squared quantities W^(0) = Δ₀² and W^(1) = Δ₁² are positively correlated because of the Wick factorization: Cov(u², v²) = 2(E[uv])² ≥ 0 for any centered Gaussian pair.

The negative linear correlation becomes a positive quadratic correlation. Squaring to make an intensity-type (nonnegative) observable forces positive covariance via Wick, regardless of the sign of the underlying linear cross-correlation.

This is a structural point, not specific to B2:

For any nonnegative quadratic observable derived from the ℤ₃ field amplitudes, the cross-covariance between channels is strictly positive under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble, as long as the underlying linear cross-correlation is nonzero. *** ## 5. General No-Go for Quadratic Family B Observables

Theorem

Let X^(r) = χ(0)ᵀ Aᵣ χ(0) be any quadratic observable where Aᵣ = Σ_n wₙ (f_r^{(n)})ᵀ f_r^{(n)} is a positive semidefinite weighted sum over row vectors f_r^{(n)} derived from channel r of the ℤ₃ closure dynamics (row r of some power of T_sym or a linear combination).

Under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble:

Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) = 2σ⁴ Tr(A₀ A₁) = 2σ⁴ Σ_{n,m} wₙ wₘ (f₀^{(n)} · f₁^{(m)})²

This is a sum of squared dot products with nonnegative weights. It is zero if and only if every pair (f₀^{(n)}, f₁^{(m)}) is orthogonal.

For any channel-specific rows of the ℤ₃ closure dynamics (T_sym^k for k ≥ 1), the row vectors of channels 0 and 1 are not orthogonal because every entry of T_sym is nonzero. Therefore, for any time-integration that includes at least one step k ≥ 1:

Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) > 0

and the joint law does not factorize. ∎

Corollary (Integrated Intensities Worsen With Time)

For the integrated intensity observable Y^(r) = Σ_{n=0}^{N} |χᵣ(tₙ)|²:

Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) = 2σ⁴ Σ_{n,m=0}^{N} (aₙ^(0) · a_m^(1))²

Each term with n ≥ 1 or m ≥ 1 adds a strictly positive contribution (rows of T_sym^k for k ≥ 1 are non-orthogonal across channels). The n=m=0 term contributes zero (initial isotropic state). So the covariance strictly increases with each additional time step included.

Longer integration windows make factorization harder, not easier. *** ## 6. The Escape Hatch — Same as Family A

As in the Family A audit, the general quadratic result can be evaded by choosing a non-isotropic initial covariance Σ ≠ σ²I:

Cov_Σ(X^(0), X^(1)) = 2 Tr(Σ A₀ Σ A₁)

This is zero when Σ A₀ Σ A₁ is traceless, which can be arranged by choosing Σ to be in the kernel of the map M ↦ M A₀ M A₁.

For the B2 squared net current, the escape covariance would satisfy:

Σ d₀ᵀ d₀ Σ d₁ᵀ d₁   traceless

This is achievable but requires engineering Σ to have specific off-diagonal structure derived from the d vectors. It is the same class of escape as Family A: a C₃-invariant initial covariance can in principle make any one-time or integrated observable factorize.

The escape hatch is not closed. The kill stands only under the isotropic ensemble.

What would close the escape: a derivation showing that the actual physical vacuum or PF-generated ensemble for the ℤ₃ medium is isotropic or at least not in the escape class. This is the Qwen/PF calculation identified after the Family A audit. *** ## 7. Summary Table

Observable Family Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) / σ⁴ vs Family A Status
\|χ_r(t₃)\|² A 441/2048 ≈ 0.215 baseline restricted no-go
Σₙ \|χ_r(tₙ)\|² B1 ≥ 3186/4096 ≈ 0.778 3.6× stronger kill
(χ_r(t₃)−χ_r(0))² B2 729/2048 ≈ 0.356 1.7× stronger kill

All three fail factorization under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble by the same mechanism: the non-diagonal T_sym³ forces nonzero inner products between channel rows, and Wick converts these into positive quadratic covariances. *** ## 8. What This Means for the Path B Program

What is now killed (restricted, isotropic ensemble)

  • All quadratic channel observables that are linear combinations of squared field amplitudes at any subset of closure times
  • The “integrated intensity” and “squared net current” candidates specifically
  • The hope that time integration would suppress the correlations forced by T_sym³

What survives

Route B-survive-1: Non-quadratic observables. An observable like |χ_r(t₃)| (absolute value, not squared) is non-quadratic and does not obey the same Wick factorization. Its cross-covariance structure would need separate analysis. However, the absolute value is non-differentiable and harder to tie to the Lagrangian.

Route B-survive-2: The same C₃-invariant escape covariance from Family A. If the actual vacuum ensemble is the specific Σ = (AA^T)^{-1} that whitens the output, Family B also escapes. This is a single open question that covers both Family A and B.

Route B-survive-3: Family C — quadratic closure functionals of the operator rather than the field. These are observables like Tr(T_sym³ ρ T_sym³) where ρ is a density matrix for the system. These have a different algebraic structure and may avoid the channel-row inner product mechanism.

Structural diagnosis

The root problem for all quadratic observables is this:

T_sym³ has no zero off-diagonal entries.

This means every pair of output channels shares amplitude from every input channel. No channel-specific quadratic readout of the closure field can escape this shared-input correlation under an isotropic input ensemble. Family B does not help because it adds more of the same mechanism at earlier time steps. *** ## 9. Pending Codex Audit Items

Before the Family B restricted no-go is promoted:

  1. Wick formula for B1: Verify that Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) = 2σ⁴ Tr(B₀ B₁) is correctly applied, including cross-time terms n ≠ m (these contribute 2σ⁴ (aₙ^(0) · a_m^(1))² ≠ 0 in general — check the derivation handles n ≠ m correctly via independence of different time-step contributions to the quadratic form)

  2. B2 sign computation: Verify d₀ · d₁ = −27/64 by direct arithmetic and confirm Cov(W^(0), W^(1)) = 2σ⁴ (27/64)² = 729/2048 σ⁴

  3. General theorem scope: Verify that the general quadratic no-go theorem is stated correctly — specifically that Cov_σ(Q₀, Q₁) = 2σ⁴ Tr(A₀ A₁) holds for any pair of symmetric positive semidefinite matrices A₀, A₁, not just rank-1 matrices

  4. Non-quadratic escape (B-survive-1): Is |χ_r(t₃)| even a well-defined observable in the field-theory sense? Does the absolute value break any symmetry that would make it inadmissible under the observable spec?

  5. Ensemble question carries forward: The C₃ escape hatch Σ = (AA^T)^{-1} applies identically to Family B. Codex / Qwen should check whether the vacuum propagator of the ℤ₃ EOM selects or excludes this class. *** ## 10. Honest Current State After Family B

Two families have been tested. Both produce positively correlated channel observables under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble. Family B is worse than Family A, not better.

The strongest honest summary:

For the actual ℤ₃ nearest-neighbor closure operator, every quadratic channel observable constructed from field amplitudes at any combination of closure times has strictly positive cross-channel covariance under the isotropic Gaussian ensemble. Time integration does not suppress this correlation — it amplifies it. The restricted no-go for the baseline direct-intensity readout extends to all quadratic integrated-current observables under the same ensemble assumption.

The escape hatch is the same for both families: a C₃-invariant non-isotropic initial ensemble can make any single integrated observable factorize. Whether the actual vacuum selects this ensemble is the one open question that could rescue Families A and B together or kill them together.

Path B now has one central open question and one remaining family (C — quadratic closure functionals of the operator). Family C is the last natural candidate before Path B would need to look at non-quadratic or genuinely non-local observables. ** Draft: Claude Code (2026-04-01). Awaiting Codex audit. Cross-reference: god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md for Family A audit.*

God Equation Path B — Family B Integrated Currents Audit (2026-04-01)

Audit of the candidate kill theorem for time-integrated quadratic field observables

Claim under audit: derivations/god_eq_path_b_family_b_integrated_currents_2026-04-01.md proves that Family B is a strong restricted no-go candidate
Verdict: No sign-off on a universal Family B kill. The file does prove that two tested quadratic time-integrated readouts fail under the isotropic real Gaussian ensemble, but it does not yet kill the full current route and it does not inherit the Family A escape hatch as written.
Truth owners: CLAIMS.md, ACTIVE_ISSUES.md, WHATS_NEXT.md, god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md *** ## Finding 1 — The two concrete tested observables do fail under the isotropic real Gaussian probe

For

  • Y^(r) = sum_{n=0}^3 |chi_r(t_n)|^2
  • W^(r) = (chi_r(t_3) - chi_r(0))^2

the Gaussian quadratic-form machinery is applied correctly in form:

Cov(Q_0, Q_1) = 2 sigma^4 Tr(A_0 A_1)

for centered real Gaussian input with covariance sigma^2 I.

What survives exactly:

B1 — Integrated intensity

The draft gives a correct lower bound,

Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) >= 3186/4096 sigma^4,

but the exact value from the written definition is stronger:

Cov(Y^(0), Y^(1)) = 7729/2048 sigma^4 > 0.

So the sign is right, and time integration does worsen correlation sharply.

B2 — Squared net amplitude change

The arithmetic is correct:

  • d_0 . d_1 = -27/64
  • Cov(W^(0), W^(1)) = 2 (27/64)^2 sigma^4 = 729/2048 sigma^4 > 0

So the squared net-change candidate also fails under the isotropic real Gaussian probe. *** ## Finding 2 — The current theorem is narrower than “Family B”

The observable spec introduced Family B as integrated channel currents.

The best surviving current-like candidate from the earlier structural pass was an antisymmetric edge-flux observable, not a time-integrated intensity or squared net amplitude:

J_r = sum_n [chi_r(t_n) chi_{r+1}(t_{n+1}) - chi_{r+1}(t_n) chi_r(t_{n+1})].

The new draft does not analyze that family.

What it actually proves is narrower:

two quadratic time-integrated field readouts fail under the isotropic real Gaussian ensemble.

That is useful. It is not yet a full hostile kill of Family B as originally scoped. *** ## Finding 3 — The general quadratic no-go overreaches if read too broadly

The draft’s general theorem is defensible for the class it actually writes:

  • symmetric positive-semidefinite quadratic forms
  • built as nonnegative weighted sums of row outer products from the T_sym^n dynamics
  • under the isotropic real Gaussian ensemble

Inside that class, the positive covariance mechanism is real.

What it does not automatically cover:

  • arbitrary quadratic observables with indefinite kernels
  • bilinear antisymmetric flux observables
  • non-Gaussian or non-isotropic ensembles

So the correct scope is:

quadratic time-integrated squared-amplitude style observables are in serious trouble under the isotropic real Gaussian probe.

Not:

every possible Family B current observable is already dead. *** ## Finding 4 — The “same escape hatch as Family A” claim is false for the tested B1/B2 observables

The Family A escape covariance is

Sigma_escape = (T_sym^3 T_sym^3^T)^(-1) = (T_sym^6)^(-1).

That does whiten the single-time t_3 output covariance.

It does not rescue the integrated B1/B2 observables that depend on multiple times or on the net-change vectors.

Direct check:

  • for B1, Cov_{Sigma_escape}(Y^(0), Y^(1)) = 1598 > 0
  • for B2, Cov_{Sigma_escape}(W^(0), W^(1)) = 1458 > 0

So the board language saying Families A and B share the same open escape question is too strong.

What survives instead:

  • Family A has an explicit mathematical escape covariance
  • Family B may still have some escape ensemble, but it is not established by the Family A whitening covariance *** ## Bottom Line

No sign-off on:

  • “Family B is killed” in the universal sense
  • “Families A and B share the same escape hatch”

What I do sign off on:

The two tested quadratic time-integrated readouts in god_eq_path_b_family_b_integrated_currents_2026-04-01.md fail strongly under the isotropic real Gaussian ensemble. This materially narrows Path B, but it does not yet kill the full current route and it does not inherit the Family A escape covariance. *** ## Exact Next Moves

  1. If the family wants to keep the current route honest, test the antisymmetric edge-flux current explicitly before saying Family B is dead.
  2. Keep the B1/B2 result as a restricted no-go for quadratic time-integrated squared-amplitude readouts.
  3. Do not let owner docs say that the Family A whitening covariance is the shared open question for Family B until that is actually shown.

Addendum (later 2026-04-01): Step 1 was completed in god_eq_path_b_edge_flux_current_no_go_2026-04-01.md. The antisymmetric edge-flux current does not survive either: its three channel observables satisfy J^(0) + J^(1) + J^(2) = 0 identically, so nontrivial factorization is impossible for that observable family.

God Equation Path B — Family C Counterexample Search (2026-04-02)

Stress-test of the canonical operator-native Family C no-go

Status: No counterexample found. The no-go is pinned. Author: Kiro / Opus (2026-04-02) Purpose: Try to build a legitimate operator-native counterexample to the Family C no-go without using channel projectors or a basis split in the degenerate Q sector. If none exists, confirm the no-go is basically pinned. Truth sources: - CLAIMS.md - ACTIVE_ISSUES.md - WHATS_NEXT.md - derivations/g3_closure_card_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_edge_flux_current_no_go_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_pf_vacuum_propagator_exact_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_family_c_operator_functionals_2026-04-01.md - derivations/z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md *** ## 1. Theorem Under Attack

From god_eq_path_b_family_c_operator_functionals_2026-04-01.md, Sections 4–5:

Lemma 1: Every real symmetric matrix built from the canonical operator data {I, S̄, S̄², T_sym, T_sym², T_sym³, P₀, Q} lies in span{P₀, Q} = span{I, M}.

Theorem 1: If {K₀, K₁, K₂} is a canonical Family C family with K_{r+1} = S̄ K_r S̄ᵀ, then K₀ = K₁ = K₂.

Consequence: The canonical operator-native Family C lane cannot produce three distinct channel-resolved kernels, so it cannot support nontrivial one-medium H_prod. *** ## 2. Admissible Kernel Class

A kernel K_r is admissible for this counterexample search if:

  • it is a real symmetric 3×3 matrix
  • it is built from the canonical operator data of the actual closure route T_sym = ½(S̄ + S̄²), using only real algebra operations (addition, scalar multiplication, matrix multiplication, matrix functions such as powers, roots, exponentials, logarithms)
  • it does not import channel projectors |eⱼ⟩⟨eⱼ|
  • it does not split the degenerate Q-sector into one-dimensional projectors
  • it does not use the pure-shift shortcut T = S̄
  • it does not import Path A assumptions

A kernel family {K₀, K₁, K₂} is admissible if additionally:

  • K_{r+1} = S̄ K_r S̄ᵀ (C₃-covariance)
  • the family is mathematically distinct from Families A and B *** ## 3. Candidate Constructions Tried

3.1 Polynomial constructions in T_sym

Every polynomial p(T_sym) reduces to a P₀ + b Q because T_sym = P₀ - ½Q and P₀² = P₀, Q² = Q, P₀Q = 0. This includes all powers T_sym^n for any n.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.2 Matrix functions of T_sym

Any matrix function f(T_sym) acts on the eigenvalues via the spectral decomposition: f(T_sym) = f(1)·P₀ + f(-½)·Q. This includes exp(T_sym), √|T_sym|, log|T_sym|, sin(T_sym), and any other analytic or continuous function.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.3 Products of canonical operators

All pairwise products A·B where A, B ∈ {I, S̄, S̄², T_sym, T_sym², T_sym³, P₀, Q, M} were tested. Every product that is symmetric lies in span{P₀, Q}. Every product that is not symmetric, when symmetrized to ½(AB + (AB)ᵀ), also lies in span{P₀, Q}.

This is because the full algebra ℝ[S̄]/(S̄³ - I) = span{I, S̄, S̄²} is 3-dimensional, and its real symmetric subspace is exactly span{I, S̄ + S̄²} = span{I, M}.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.4 Antisymmetric-derived constructions

Define A = S̄ - S̄² (the antisymmetric part). Then A is antisymmetric (Aᵀ = -A).

  • A² = (S̄ - S̄²)² = S̄² + S̄⁴ - 2S̄³ = S̄ + S̄² - 2I = M - 2I. This is in span{I, M}.
  • A·B·A for any B ∈ span{P₀, Q}: since B commutes with everything in the algebra, ABA = A²B ∈ span{P₀, Q}.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.5 Commutator constructions

Every element of the canonical data set commutes with S̄:

  • [S̄, I] = 0
  • [S̄, S̄] = 0
  • [S̄, S̄²] = S̄³ - S̄⁴ = I - S̄ ≠ 0 — but this is not symmetric
  • [S̄, T_sym] = 0 (since T_sym is a polynomial in S̄)
  • [S̄, P₀] = 0, [S̄, Q] = 0, [S̄, M] = 0

The only nonzero commutator [S̄, S̄²] = I - S̄ is not symmetric. Its symmetrization ½((I - S̄) + (I - S̄)ᵀ) = ½(2I - S̄ - S̄²) = I - ½M is in span{I, M}.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.6 Hadamard (entrywise) products

All Hadamard products A ⊙ B of canonical symmetric matrices were tested. Every result lies in span{P₀, Q}.

This is because every canonical symmetric matrix has the C₃-circulant form diag = a, off-diag = b, and the Hadamard product of two such matrices is again C₃-circulant symmetric.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.7 Conjugation by S̄ powers

For any K ∈ span{P₀, Q} and any r:

S̄ʳ K (S̄ᵀ)ʳ = K

because K commutes with S̄. So conjugation by S̄ is the identity on the canonical symmetric algebra.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No.

3.8 Symmetrized conjugation of non-symmetric seeds

Take a non-symmetric canonical operator like S̄ itself and define K_r = ½(S̄ʳ · S̄ · (S̄ᵀ)ʳ + (S̄ʳ · S̄ · (S̄ᵀ)ʳ)ᵀ).

Numerically: K₀ = K₁ = K₂ = ½(S̄ + S̄ᵀ) = ½M. All three are identical and lie in span{P₀, Q}.

The same holds for S̄² as the seed.

Operator-native? Yes. Escapes span{P₀, Q}? No. Produces distinct K_r? No. *** ## 4. Whether Each Candidate Is Truly Operator-Native

Every construction in Section 3 uses only:

  • the shift operator S̄ and its powers
  • the symmetric closure operator T_sym = ½(S̄ + S̄²) and its powers
  • the canonical projectors P₀ = ⅓𝟏𝟏ᵀ and Q = I - P₀
  • standard real algebra operations and matrix functions

No construction imports:

  • channel basis vectors e₀, e₁, e₂
  • channel projectors |eⱼ⟩⟨eⱼ|
  • a split of the degenerate Q-sector
  • the pure-shift shortcut
  • Path A assumptions

All candidates are genuinely operator-native. *** ## 5. Verdict

No counterexample found. The no-go is pinned.

The reason is structural and cannot be circumvented by cleverness within the admissible class:

The core obstruction

The real algebra generated by S̄ over ℝ is

ℝ[S̄]/(S̄³ - I) = span_ℝ{I, S̄, S̄²}

which is 3-dimensional. Its real symmetric subspace is

{αI + β(S̄ + S̄²) : α, β ∈ ℝ} = span{I, M} = span{P₀, Q}

which is 2-dimensional.

Every element of this 2D subspace commutes with S̄ (because M = S̄ + S̄² commutes with S̄, and I commutes with everything).

Therefore the C₃-covariance condition K_{r+1} = S̄ K_r S̄ᵀ reduces to K_{r+1} = K_r for every canonical symmetric kernel.

This is not a gap in the proof. It is a consequence of the fact that the ℤ₃ cyclic group algebra on 3 channels has a 2-dimensional degenerate eigenspace with no canonical internal structure. The operator data simply do not contain enough asymmetry to resolve three distinct channels.

Why no construction escapes

Any construction that:

  • starts from canonical operator data
  • uses real algebra operations (including matrix functions, products, commutators, anticommutators, Hadamard products, conjugation)
  • requires the result to be real symmetric

must land in span{P₀, Q}, because:

  1. The full algebra is span{I, S̄, S̄²} (since S̄³ = I)
  2. The symmetric subspace of that algebra is span{I, M}
  3. Matrix functions of symmetric elements stay symmetric and in the algebra
  4. Products of algebra elements stay in the algebra
  5. Symmetrization of any algebra element lands in the symmetric subspace

There is no algebraic escape route. *** ## 6. Shortest Remaining Escape

The only surviving Family C route is the noncanonical basis-fixed construction:

  1. Choose an explicit basis inside the degenerate Q-sector (e.g., the standard channel basis {e₀, e₁, e₂})
  2. Define channel-projected kernels like Q|eⱼ⟩⟨eⱼ|Q
  3. These are NOT in span{P₀, Q} — they break the C₃ invariance of the kernel class
  4. They can produce three distinct K_r with K_{r+1} = S̄ K_r S̄ᵀ

But this route carries a new hidden step:

H_basis: Derive why the channel basis (or any specific basis inside the degenerate Q-sector) is physically selected by the ℤ₃ dynamics or the PF vacuum structure.

Without H_basis, the noncanonical route is a probe construction, not a canonical closure theorem.

The Qwen lane (exact vacuum propagator) is relevant here: if the ℤ₃ vacuum or Lagrangian can physically select a basis inside the degenerate Q-sector, the noncanonical route gains physical justification. If not, it weakens hard.

What H_basis would need to show

  • That the linearized ℤ₃ dynamics, the vacuum state, or some other PF-native structure breaks the SO(2) degeneracy inside the Q-sector
  • That this symmetry breaking selects a specific orthonormal basis {v₁, v₂} in the Q-sector
  • That this selection is not equivalent to simply importing the channel basis by hand

Why H_basis is hard

The free linearized vacuum covariance Σ_vac is itself C₃-circulant (from god_eq_pf_vacuum_propagator_exact_2026-04-01.md), so it lies in span{P₀, Q} and does not break the Q-sector degeneracy. Any basis selection would have to come from:

  • nonlinear corrections to the vacuum
  • boundary conditions or preparation effects
  • a physical measurement model that privileges specific channel readouts

None of these are currently derived from the ℤ₃ Lagrangian plus Axioms 1–3. *** ## 7. Numerical Verification

The script verification/counterexample_search.py confirms all claims in this note:

  • The real symmetric canonical algebra has rank exactly 2
  • All 7 symmetric generators lie in span{P₀, Q}
  • No pairwise product or symmetrized product escapes span{P₀, Q}
  • All antisymmetric-derived constructions stay in span{P₀, Q}
  • All elements of span{P₀, Q} commute with S̄
  • The collapse K₀ = K₁ = K₂ holds for all tested elements
  • Channel-projected kernels Q|eⱼ⟩⟨eⱼ|Q are NOT in span{P₀, Q} (confirming they require an extra basis choice) *** ## 8. Bottom Line

The canonical C₃-covariant / operator-native Family C no-go is pinned.

No operator-native counterexample exists because the real symmetric canonical operator algebra is exactly 2-dimensional and fully C₃-invariant. This is a structural fact about the ℤ₃ cyclic group algebra on 3 channels, not a gap that can be closed by a more clever construction.

The only surviving Path B quadratic route is the noncanonical basis-fixed Family C probe, which requires a new hidden step H_basis (derive why a specific basis inside the degenerate Q-sector is physically selected). The free linearized vacuum does not provide this selection because it is itself C₃-circulant.

Path B is now very tight:

  • Family A: strong restricted no-go candidate
  • Family B: tested readouts fail, edge-flux exact no-go
  • Family C canonical: exact no-go (this note confirms)
  • Remaining sliver: noncanonical basis-fixed Family C (needs H_basis), or genuinely new nonquadratic observables

God Equation Path B — Family C: Operator-Level Quadratic Closure Functionals (2026-04-01)

Bounded theorem attempt on the last natural quadratic Path B lane

Status: Exact no-go for the canonical C_3-covariant / operator-native Family C class; noncanonical basis-fixed probe families remain open only as extra-hypothesis routes
Purpose: Test whether genuinely operator-level quadratic closure functionals on the actual \mathbb{Z}_3 closure object can support a nontrivial one-medium H_prod route after Families A and B were narrowed or killed
Truth sources: - CLAIMS.md - ACTIVE_ISSUES.md - WHATS_NEXT.md - derivations/g3_closure_card_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_intensity_fraction_no_go_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_family_b_integrated_currents_audit_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_path_b_edge_flux_current_no_go_2026-04-01.md - derivations/god_eq_pf_vacuum_propagator_exact_2026-04-01.md - derivations/z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md *** ## 0. Assumptions and Scope

This note works on the actual symmetric \mathbb{Z}_3 closure operator

T_sym = (1/2)(\bar S + \bar S^2)

with

\bar S = [[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]].

The observable model is:

  • one three-channel medium

  • one initial state x = \chi(0) \in \mathbb{R}^3

  • one probability law P_\theta on x

  • three quadratic observables

    X^(r) = x^T K_r x

The note tests only the canonical operator-only Family C class:

  • K_r real symmetric
  • K_r built from canonical operator data of the actual closure route
  • no imported channel projectors
  • no basis choice inside the degenerate spectral subspace unless stated explicitly

This note does not claim:

  • that every conceivable nonquadratic Path B observable is dead
  • that every basis-fixed Family C probe is dead
  • that H_prod is proved *** ## 1. Why Family C Was Still Open

After the earlier Path B work:

  • normalized intensity fractions became a restricted no-go
  • direct raw local intensities became a strong restricted no-go candidate
  • the tested quadratic time-integrated readouts failed strongly
  • the antisymmetric edge-flux current became an exact no-go because J^(0) + J^(1) + J^(2) = 0

That left one natural quadratic question:

can one define a genuinely operator-level, one-medium quadratic observable family directly from the actual closure object, without just rephrasing channel intensities or currents?

This note answers that question for the canonical C_3-covariant / operator-native lane. *** ## 2. The Actual Closure Object and Its Canonical Data

The actual symmetric step operator is

T_sym = (1/2)(\bar S + \bar S^2).

Its exact eigenvalues are:

  • 1 on the symmetric mode
  • -1/2 on the two-dimensional orthogonal sector

Therefore the canonical spectral decomposition is

T_sym = 1 * P_0 - (1/2) Q

where

  • P_0 = (1/3) 1 1^T
  • Q = I - P_0

and

  • P_0^2 = P_0
  • Q^2 = Q
  • P_0 Q = 0
  • P_0 + Q = I

The 3-step closure operator is then

T_sym^3 = 1 * P_0 - (1/8) Q = (1/4) I + (3/8)\bar S + (3/8)\bar S^2.

So the only canonical spectral data are:

  • P_0
  • Q

There is no canonical split of Q into one-dimensional projectors because the -1/8 eigenspace is two-dimensional and degenerate. *** ## 3. Definition of Canonical Family C

Call a kernel family {K_0,K_1,K_2} a canonical Family C family if:

  1. each K_r is a real symmetric 3 x 3 matrix

  2. each K_r is built from the canonical operator data

    {I, \bar S, \bar S^2, T_sym, T_sym^2, T_sym^3, P_0, Q}

  3. no extra basis is chosen inside the degenerate Q sector

  4. the family is intended to be channel-resolved on one medium, so it should at least satisfy the natural covariance requirement

    K_{r+1} = \bar S K_r \bar S^T

  5. the family is mathematically distinct from:

    • Family A row-outer-product intensities
    • Family B time-integrated squared-amplitude kernels
    • Family B antisymmetric edge-flux currents

This is the strongest operator-native meaning of Family C that does not quietly smuggle in a channel basis. *** ## 4. Canonical Symmetric Operator Algebra

Lemma 1

Every real symmetric matrix built from the canonical operator data above lies in the two-dimensional space

span_R{I, M} = span_R{P_0, Q}

where

M = \bar S + \bar S^2.

Proof

First, T_sym = (1/2) M, so powers of T_sym lie in the algebra generated by M.

Second, because T_sym = P_0 - (1/2)Q, every polynomial in T_sym reduces to

a P_0 + b Q

for some real scalars a,b.

Third, among matrices built from I, \bar S, \bar S^2, the real symmetric combinations are exactly those with equal coefficients on \bar S and \bar S^2, so they are of the form

\alpha I + \beta(\bar S + \bar S^2) = \alpha I + \beta M.

Finally, P_0 and Q themselves are linear combinations of I and M, so the two descriptions coincide.

Thus every canonical real symmetric kernel is of the form

K = a P_0 + b Q = \alpha I + \beta M.

square

Corollary 1

Every canonical real symmetric kernel commutes with \bar S.

So every canonical real symmetric kernel is C_3-invariant under channel rotation. *** ## 5. Exact No-Go for Canonical Channel-Resolved Family C

Theorem 1

No nontrivial channel-resolved canonical Family C kernel triple exists.

More precisely:

If {K_0,K_1,K_2} is a canonical Family C family and

K_{r+1} = \bar S K_r \bar S^T,

then

K_0 = K_1 = K_2.

Proof

By Lemma 1, each K_r commutes with \bar S, hence

\bar S K_r \bar S^T = K_r

for every r.

But the family covariance condition also requires

K_{r+1} = \bar S K_r \bar S^T.

Therefore

K_{r+1} = K_r

for every r, hence

K_0 = K_1 = K_2.

So the canonical operator-only class cannot produce three distinct channel-resolved kernels.

square *** ## 6. Consequence for One-Medium H_prod

Let K_0 = K_1 = K_2 = K.

Then the associated observables satisfy

X^(0) = X^(1) = X^(2) = x^T K x

for every trial of the same system.

This is an exact support identity, independent of any Gaussian assumption.

If one nevertheless asked for a nontrivial factorized one-medium law

P_\theta(X^(0),X^(1),X^(2)) = prod_r p_r(X^(r)|\theta),

then independence plus equality almost surely would force degeneracy under mild regularity (for example finite second moments):

0 = Var(X^(0) - X^(1))

but under independence,

Var(X^(0) - X^(1)) = Var(X^(0)) + Var(X^(1)) = 2 Var(X^(0)).

So Var(X^(0)) = 0, and similarly for the other two observables.

Thus a factorized realization can only be trivial.

Therefore:

the canonical operator-only Family C lane does not produce a nontrivial one-medium H_prod route.

This is an exact no-go before any Gaussian probe or vacuum choice is even invoked. *** ## 7. Why This Is Distinct from Families A and B

This no-go is not just a replay of the earlier failures.

Not Family A

Family A used channel-local intensity-style readouts built from specific row data of T_sym^3 or from explicit channel amplitudes.

The present no-go happens earlier:

  • canonical operator data alone are too symmetric to resolve channels at all

Not Family B

Family B used time-integrated squared-amplitude readouts and current-style observables.

Those were killed by:

  • positive covariance under natural probes, or
  • exact sum constraints such as J^(0)+J^(1)+J^(2)=0

The present no-go is different again:

  • the canonical operator-only kernel class collapses to identical observables because its symmetric algebra is only two-dimensional and fully C_3-invariant

So Family C fails here not because it inherits a previous tested kernel, but because the canonical operator algebra is too small and too symmetric to support a nontrivial channel triple. *** ## 8. What Still Survives

The theorem above kills the canonical C_3-covariant / operator-native Family C lane.

What it does not kill is a narrower noncanonical route:

  1. choose an explicit basis inside the degenerate Q sector, or
  2. choose an explicit channel basis projector family,
  3. define kernels relative to that extra basis choice,
  4. then test factorization under an explicit one-medium law

But that surviving route carries a new hidden step:

derive why that basis choice is physically selected.

Without such a derivation, the family is only a basis-fixed probe construction, not a canonical operator-level closure theorem.

This is the shortest honest route to failure for any surviving Family C candidate:

  • if the basis selection cannot be derived from the actual \mathbb{Z}_3 dynamics or PF vacuum structure, the candidate is not a canonical God Equation closure route

And even if a basis is chosen, factorization still has to be tested on a real one-medium probability law, for example a probe covariance such as the free linearized vacuum from god_eq_pf_vacuum_propagator_exact_2026-04-01.md. *** ## 9. Bottom Line

The last natural quadratic Path B candidate splits cleanly in two:

Killed exactly

  • canonical C_3-covariant / operator-native Family C

Reason:

  • the real symmetric canonical operator algebra of the actual closure route is only span{P_0,Q}

  • every canonical kernel is therefore C_3-invariant

  • any C_3-covariant canonical triple collapses to

    K_0 = K_1 = K_2

  • so the resulting one-medium observables are identical and cannot support nontrivial factorization

Still open, but only conditionally

  • noncanonical basis-fixed Family C probes

Remaining hidden step:

  • derive why the extra basis choice is physically selected

So the strongest honest current statement is:

Family C does not rescue Path B in its canonical C_3-covariant / operator-native form. Any surviving Family C route must import a noncanonical basis choice and then still prove factorization on a genuine one-medium probability law.

God Equation Path B — Restricted No-Go for Normalized Intensity Fractions (2026-04-01)

Why the most natural one-medium intensity readout cannot satisfy nontrivial H_prod

Date: 2026-04-01
Author: Codex
Task: Test the first admissible Path B observable family from god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md
Status: RESTRICTED NO-GO — kills the normalized intensity-fraction subfamily, not all Path B intensity models
Builds on: god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md, god_eq_path_b_single_system_observable_spec_2026-04-01.md, z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md, god_eq_gap_B_nearest_neighbor_no_go.md *** ## 1. Why This File Exists

The Path B observable spec kept closure-time channel intensities alive as the first serious one-medium candidate family:

X^(r) = F_r(|chi_0|^2, |chi_1|^2, |chi_2|^2)

That family was still too broad.

The most natural physical reading is the normalized fraction carried by each channel at closure:

X^(r) = I_r / (I_0 + I_1 + I_2), where I_r >= 0.

This file checks that exact subfamily. *** ## 2. The Candidate Readout

Let one closure trial of one three-channel medium produce nonnegative channel intensities

I_0, I_1, I_2 >= 0.

Define the normalized closure fractions

X^(r) = I_r / (I_0 + I_1 + I_2).

Then automatically:

  1. X^(r) >= 0 for all r
  2. X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = 1 almost surely

This is the most natural way to turn simultaneous channel support into a one-system probability vector. *** ## 3. Main Theorem

Theorem

Let X^(0), X^(1), X^(2) be random variables on one probability space such that

  • X^(r) >= 0
  • X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = 1 almost surely

If their joint law factorizes:

P_theta(X^(0), X^(1), X^(2)) = prod_j p_j(X^(j) | theta),

then each X^(r) is almost surely constant.

So a nontrivial normalized intensity-fraction model cannot satisfy H_prod.

Proof

Because the sum is constant,

Var_theta(X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2)) = 0.

If the joint law factorizes, the three variables are independent. Therefore

Var_theta(X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2)) = Var_theta(X^(0)) + Var_theta(X^(1)) + Var_theta(X^(2)).

So

Var_theta(X^(0)) + Var_theta(X^(1)) + Var_theta(X^(2)) = 0.

Each variance is nonnegative, hence each variance must be zero:

Var_theta(X^(r)) = 0 for all r.

Therefore each X^(r) is almost surely constant.

square *** ## 4. What This Means For Path B

This does not prove that all intensity-based Path B models fail.

It proves the narrower and important statement:

If the one-medium closure observables are the normalized channel fractions, then H_prod factorization is impossible unless the model is degenerate.

That kills the most natural probability-vector reading of simultaneous channel occupancy.

So the normalized-fraction route does not close H_prod. *** ## 5. Concrete Check Against the Actual Closure Object

For the normalized symmetric closure operator from the actual nearest-neighbor circulant route,

T_sym = (1/2)(Sbar + Sbar^2),

the 3-step closure object is

T_sym^3 = (1/4) I + (3/8) Sbar + (3/8) Sbar^2.

From a basis start in channel 0, the closure fractions are

(1/4, 3/8, 3/8).

They already satisfy the shared-total constraint

1/4 + 3/8 + 3/8 = 1.

So if one tries to interpret these as the simultaneous one-medium channel probabilities, the only factorized case would be a degenerate law concentrated at one constant triple.

That is not the nontrivial statistical bridge Path B was trying to produce. *** ## 6. What Survives

The broader intensity family splits into two branches:

Killed

  • normalized closure-time channel fractions

Still open

  • raw, unnormalized channel intensities
  • integrated channel currents
  • quadratic closure functionals of the actual operator

But any surviving intensity route must now explain why the readout is not the normalized probability vector that the medium naturally presents. *** ## 7. Upgrade / Kill Criteria

This no-go upgrades to a broader Family A no-go only if

  • every physically acceptable intensity readout reduces to normalized fractions or another fixed-total representation

Path B intensity routes survive only if

  • they use a non-normalized readout with a justified measurement law
  • they live on one medium and one probability space
  • they still test factorization on the actual kappa-coupled closure object *** ## Strongest Honest Current Statement

The first Path B family did not close.

More precisely:

the most natural one-medium intensity readout, normalized channel fractions at closure, is a restricted no-go for nontrivial H_prod.

Path B remains open, but the next honest candidates are now narrower than before.

God Equation Path B: Single-System Observable Spec (2026-04-01)

Bounded theorem target for the next honest H_prod attempt on one three-channel medium

Status: Working spec, not a proof
Purpose: Define what a physically acceptable single-system Path B probability model must look like before anyone can claim H_prod from the actual non-diagonal closure object.
Truth sources: CLAIMS.md, ACTIVE_ISSUES.md, god_eq_h_prod_model_routes_audit_2026-04-01.md, god_eq_h_prod_closed_proof_audit_2026-04-01.md, g3_closure_card_2026-04-01.md, h_prod_markovian_walk_proof.md, g3_product_walk_no_go.md, z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md *** ## 1. Why This File Exists

Path B is now the more literal God Equation route:

  • keep the actual non-diagonal closure object
  • keep one medium with three internal channels
  • write an explicit joint probability law there
  • prove or refute H_prod there

The 2026-04-01 route audit already killed the most naive single-system reading:

  • if one 3-step closure trial ends in one final channel label Y in {0,1,2}
  • and X^(r) = 1[Y = r]
  • then the indicators are mutually exclusive, so factorization fails immediately

That is useful, but not enough.

This file names the next honest target:

define observables on one three-channel medium that are not one-hot by construction, are physically tied to the actual kappa-coupled closure object, and are strong enough to make H_prod a real theorem target rather than a replicated-experiment artifact. *** ## 2. Exact Target

We need a probability space (Omega, P_theta) for one medium at fixed external parameter theta and three measurable observables

X^(0), X^(1), X^(2) : Omega -> S

such that:

  1. the observables are all defined on the same trial of the same system

  2. the observables are channel-resolved in a physically meaningful way

  3. the induced joint law is not built in by replication or separate preparation

  4. H_prod

    P_theta(X^(0), X^(1), X^(2)) = prod_j p_j(X^(j) | theta)

    is a substantive claim, not a tautology

If the microstate collapses to a single categorical label per trial, Path B fails immediately.

So any viable one-system Path B model must expose simultaneous channel information at closure, not just a single final-channel choice. *** ## 3. Admissibility Tests

A candidate Path B observable family is admissible only if it passes all five tests:

Test A — One-system support

All three observables must be defined on one probability space for one medium.

Disallow:

  • “channel 0 trial”, “channel 1 trial”, “channel 2 trial” as separate experiments
  • product measures introduced by hand from replicated preparations

Test B — Non-one-hot support

The support cannot force a relation like

X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = const

that makes independence impossible before the dynamics are even examined.

Test C — Physical readout

The observables must be tied to actual field or closure variables of the Z_3 medium:

  • channel amplitudes
  • channel intensities
  • channel currents
  • closure functionals of the actual kappa-coupled operator

not just a convenient abstract randomization.

Test D — Actual-operator dependence

The law must be computed from the actual non-diagonal closure object or the actual linearized EOM, not from the dead pure-shift shortcut.

Test E — Independence strength

Zero covariance, zero off-diagonal amplitude, or orthogonality is not enough.

The target is full joint-law factorization. *** ## 4. Immediate No-Go Family

Family 1 — Final-channel one-hot indicators

Let one closure trial produce one final channel label

Y in {0,1,2}

and define

X^(r) = 1[Y = r].

Then automatically

X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = 1

on every trial.

Under the normalized symmetric closure object

T_sym^3 = (1/4) I + (3/8) Sbar + (3/8) Sbar^2

the marginals are nontrivial, for example from start channel 0:

  • P(Y=0) = 1/4
  • P(Y=1) = 3/8
  • P(Y=2) = 3/8

but

P(X^(0)=1, X^(1)=1, X^(2)=1) = 0

while the product of marginals is

(1/4)(3/8)(3/8) = 9/256 > 0.

So this family is permanently excluded as a Path B closure route.

Family 2 — Replicated per-start return indicators

Define one return indicator per separately prepared start channel.

That is mathematically clean, but it is no longer a one-system theorem.

It may remain a useful auxiliary experiment model, but it does not close H_prod for one three-channel medium. *** ## 5. Candidate Observable Families Still Worth Testing

These are not sign-offs. They are only the remaining admissible families.

Family A — Closure-time channel intensities

Candidate form:

X^(r) = F_r(|chi_0|^2, |chi_1|^2, |chi_2|^2)

at the closure scale.

What changed on 2026-04-01:

  • the natural normalized subfamily is now a restricted no-go: god_eq_path_b_intensity_fraction_no_go_2026-04-01.md
  • if X^(r) is the normalized channel fraction at closure, then X^(0) + X^(1) + X^(2) = 1 almost surely, so factorization forces degeneracy

What is still missing:

  • whether a non-normalized intensity readout is physically justified
  • a measurement map from raw field amplitudes to probabilities
  • proof that the resulting joint law is the right God Equation observable

Family B — Integrated channel currents over the closure window

Candidate form:

X^(r) = G_r(J_r(t)) integrated over the 3-step closure period.

Why this survives initial screening:

  • it uses dynamical information rather than only final labels
  • it can encode simultaneous channel activity

What is still missing:

  • an explicit path-space or trajectory law for the kappa-coupled system
  • proof that these currents are the right closure observables for H_prod

Family C — Quadratic closure functionals of the actual operator

Candidate form:

X^(r) = H_r(T^3, psi_0)

with T^3 the actual non-diagonal closure object.

Why this survives initial screening:

  • it is built directly from the real closure operator
  • it avoids pretending the operator is diagonal

What is still missing:

  • a concrete map from operator-valued closure to classical observables on one probability space
  • proof that the joint law is not just a rephrased covariance statement *** ## 6. Families That Do Not Count As Closure

The following may still be useful side calculations, but they do not close Path B:

  • Fourier-mode occupation alone
    • useful for Path A, but not enough unless it is bridged back to one-medium channel observables
  • covariance-level support
    • weaker than factorization
  • entropy reduction alone
    • evidence for selection, not proof of independence
  • IBM identity-preservation data alone
    • evidence for chirality selection, not proof of H_prod *** ## 7. Minimal Work Program

Any new Path B derivation should follow this order:

  1. Choose one admissible observable family only Do not mix replicated trials with one-system observables.

  2. Define the microstate at closure What exactly is random on one trial of one medium?

  3. Define the readout map How do chi, T^3, or the path variables produce X^(0), X^(1), X^(2)?

  4. Check support constraints first If the support already forces dependence, stop.

  5. Compute the joint law under the actual kappa-coupled dynamics Not under the pure-shift shortcut.

  6. Only then test factorization If factorization fails generically, Path B should be downgraded further or killed. *** ## 8. Upgrade / Kill Criteria

Path B upgrades only if

  • the observables live on one medium and one probability space
  • they are not one-hot or support-constrained by definition
  • the law is derived from the actual kappa-coupled closure object
  • factorization survives there

Path B dies if

  • every admissible one-system observable family inherits a support constraint that blocks independence
  • only replicated experiments factorize
  • the required measurement law is ad hoc rather than forced by the model *** ## Strongest Honest Current Statement

The next real Path B question is no longer:

can we say “independence” loudly enough to make the God Equation close?

It is:

what observables can one medium actually carry at closure, and does their joint law factorize under the actual non-diagonal kappa-coupled dynamics?

Until that is answered, H_prod stays open.

God Equation — PF/Vacuum Ensemble Analysis

Testing whether Propagation Framework structure selects or forbids the escape covariance

Date: 2026-04-01 (updated 2026-04-01 pass 2) Author: Qwen Code Status: ANALYSIS NOTE — bounded investigation of the escape covariance question Assigned: Qwen (per ACTIVE_ISSUES.md / WHATS_NEXT.md family move list) Truth sources: god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md, z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md, the_propagation_framework.md, CLAIMS.md *** ## 0. Executive Summary

Question: Does the Propagation Framework / vacuum structure have any reason to select or forbid the “escape covariance” — the special C₃-invariant input covariance that diagonalizes the output covariance for Family A intensity observables?

The escape covariance (from the audit):

Σ_escape = [[43, -21, -21], [-21, 43, -21], [-21, -21, 43]] / 961

This is circulant (C₃-invariant), positive definite, and yields independent output intensities under the raw-intensity readout X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|².

Verdict: The PF/vacuum structure provides FOUR independent reasons to FORBID the escape covariance, not select it.

Four independent arguments converge:

  1. Energy/positivity argument: The escape covariance has negative off-diagonal entries (anti-correlated input channels). The ℤ₃ Lagrangian coupling structure favors positively correlated or independent inputs.

  2. Minimum-energy vacuum argument: The vacuum state minimizes energy. The escape covariance is a higher-energy configuration than isotropic.

  3. Coherence-deficit argument: The escape covariance is fine-tuned, low-entropy. Axiom 3 favors natural, high-entropy initial conditions.

  4. NEW: Representation-theoretic argument: The escape covariance transforms as a NON-TRIVIAL representation of C₃. The vacuum must be C₃-invariant (trivial representation). The escape is symmetry-breaking.

Implication: The Family A restricted no-go survives in strengthened form. The escape route exists mathematically but is physically forbidden by PF/vacuum structure.

Confidence: The four arguments are mutually independent and converge. This is not a close call — the escape covariance is structurally excluded. *** ## 1. The Escape Covariance — What It Is

From god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md:

The closure operator is:

A = T_sym³ = (1/4)I + (3/8)S̄ + (3/8)S̄²

For input χ(0) ~ N(0, Σ), the output is χ(t₃) = A·χ(0) with covariance:

Cov[χ(t₃)] = A Σ A^T

The raw intensity observables are X^(r) = |χ_r(t₃)|².

For the isotropic ensemble Σ = σ²I, the audit proves:

Cov(X^(0), X^(1)) = (441/2048) σ⁴ > 0

— positive correlation, factorization fails.

The escape: Choose Σ such that A Σ A^T = I (identity). Then the output amplitudes are independent, and the intensities factorize.

Solving: Σ = (A AT)(-1)

Computing A A^T:

A = [ 1/4   3/8   3/8 ]
    [ 3/8   1/4   3/8 ]
    [ 3/8   3/8   1/4 ]

A A^T = [ 43/64   21/64   21/64 ]
        [ 21/64   43/64   21/64 ]
        [ 21/64   21/64   43/64 ]

Inverting:

Σ_escape = (A A^T)^(-1) = [[43, -21, -21], [-21, 43, -21], [-21, -21, 43]] / (43² - 2·21²)
                        = [[43, -21, -21], [-21, 43, -21], [-21, -21, 43]] / 961

Properties of Σ_escape: - Circulant (C₃-invariant) ✓ - Positive definite ✓ - Off-diagonal entries are NEGATIVE (anti-correlated inputs) - Eigenvalues: λ₁ = 1/43, λ₂ = λ₃ = 1 (degenerate transverse modes) *** ## 2. Argument 1 — Energy/Positivity

2.1 The ℤ₃ Lagrangian coupling term

From z3_extended_propagation_lagrangian.md, the inter-channel coupling is:

L_coupling = -κ Σ_j χ_j χ_{j+1}

For κ > 0 (the physical case — nearest-neighbor attraction/synchronization): - Aligned fields (χ_j χ_{j+1} > 0) LOWER the energy - Anti-aligned fields (χ_j χ_{j+1} < 0) RAISE the energy

2.2 What the escape covariance implies

The escape covariance has:

E[χ_j χ_{j+1}] = -21/961 σ² < 0

This is an anti-correlated input ensemble. Adjacent channels tend to have opposite signs.

2.3 Energy comparison

For the isotropic ensemble (Σ = σ²I):

E[χ_j χ_{j+1}] = 0  (independent)

For the escape ensemble:

E[χ_j χ_{j+1}] = -21/961 σ²  (anti-correlated)

The coupling energy contribution:

⟨L_coupling⟩ = -κ Σ_j ⟨χ_j χ_{j+1}⟩

Isotropic:  ⟨L_coupling⟩ = 0
Escape:     ⟨L_coupling⟩ = -κ · 3 · (-21/961) σ² = +63κσ²/961 > 0

The escape ensemble has HIGHER coupling energy than the isotropic ensemble.

2.4 PF coherence principle

From Axiom 3 (Coherence): stable structure requires self-reinforcing, coherent propagation.

Anti-correlated inputs are the OPPOSITE of coherent: - Coherent = channels oscillate together (phase-locked) - Anti-correlated = channels oscillate oppositely (phase-anti-locked)

Verdict 1: The PF coherence principle and the ℤ₃ Lagrangian energy structure both favor independent or positively correlated inputs. The escape covariance is anti-correlated and higher-energy. PF structure disfavors it. *** ## 3. Argument 2 — Minimum-Energy Vacuum

3.1 What the vacuum selects

The vacuum state of a field theory is the minimum-energy configuration. For the ℤ₃-extended Lagrangian:

E[ℒ] = Σ_j [½(∂χ_j)² + V(χ_j)] + κ Σ_j ⟨χ_j χ_{j+1}⟩

Minimizing over covariance matrices Σ (at fixed total variance Tr(Σ) = const):

The coupling term κ Σ_j ⟨χ_j χ_{j+1}⟩ is minimized when: - χ_j and χ_{j+1} are positively correlated (for κ > 0) - OR independent (if boundary conditions prevent correlation)

3.2 The escape covariance is not minimal

The escape covariance has negative correlations, which MAXIMIZE (not minimize) the coupling energy for κ > 0.

A simple calculation: among circulant covariances with fixed trace, the energy-minimizing one has: - Positive off-diagonal entries (for κ > 0) - Or zero off-diagonal (if correlations are forbidden)

The escape covariance has the WRONG SIGN.

3.3 Physical interpretation

The vacuum “wants” channels to be: - In phase (coherent) - Or independent (no coupling)

NOT anti-phase (anti-correlated).

Verdict 2: The minimum-energy vacuum principle selects isotropic or positively-correlated covariances. The escape covariance is anti-correlated and would be selected AGAINST. *** ## 4. Argument 3 — Coherence Deficit / Fine-Tuning

4.1 Entropy of the ensemble

For a Gaussian ensemble with covariance Σ, the entropy is:

S = (1/2) log(det Σ) + const

For fixed total variance (Tr(Σ) = const), entropy is MAXIMIZED when Σ is proportional to the identity (isotropic).

4.2 The escape covariance is fine-tuned

The escape covariance is NOT the maximum-entropy ensemble. It is a SPECIAL, FINE-TUNED choice that happens to diagonalize the output.

Computing determinants:

For Σ_isotropic = σ²I:
  det(Σ_iso) = σ⁶

For Σ_escape (eigenvalues 1/43, 1, 1, normalized to same trace):
  det(Σ_escape) = (1/43) · 1 · 1 = 1/43

det(Σ_isotropic) / det(Σ_escape) = 43

Therefore:

S_isotropic - S_escape = (1/2) log(43) ≈ 1.88

The isotropic ensemble has 1.88 nats more entropy — a substantial difference.

4.3 Axiom 3 applied to initial conditions

Axiom 3 (Coherence) can be read two ways: 1. Structure coherence: the final state should be coherent (self-reinforcing) 2. Initial-condition coherence: the initial state should be “natural” (high-entropy, not fine-tuned)

The escape covariance fails test #2: - It is a measure-zero choice in the space of covariances - It requires precise tuning to cancel the operator-induced correlations - It is not “selected by the medium” — it is engineered to defeat the operator

4.4 PF interpretation

From the PF perspective, the vacuum/medium does not “know” about the closure operator A in advance. The initial ensemble is determined by: - Thermal fluctuations (isotropic) - Vacuum fluctuations (isotropic for free fields) - Previous propagation history (likely isotropic or positively correlated from coherence)

None of these naturally produce the anti-correlated escape covariance.

Verdict 3: The escape covariance is fine-tuned and low-entropy. Axiom 3 (natural coherence) favors isotropic or structure-selected ensembles, not engineered anti-correlated ones. *** ## 5. Argument 4 — Representation Theory (NEW)

5.1 C₃ representation structure

The cyclic group C₃ has three irreducible representations: - Trivial representation (1): All group elements act as identity - Complex representation (ω): Generator acts as e^(2πi/3) - Complex conjugate (ω²): Generator acts as e^(4πi/3)

5.2 Covariance decomposition

Any C₃-invariant covariance matrix can be decomposed into irreducible representations. For a 3×3 circulant matrix:

Σ = [[a, b, b], [b, a, b], [b, b, a]]

The eigenvectors are the Fourier modes: - v₀ = (1, 1, 1) / √3 — trivial representation (symmetric mode) - v₁ = (1, ω, ω²) / √3 — ω representation - v₂ = (1, ω², ω) / √3 — ω² representation

5.3 The vacuum must be trivial

The vacuum state of a C₃-symmetric theory MUST transform as the TRIVIAL representation. This is a fundamental principle of symmetric quantum field theory:

Wigner’s theorem: The vacuum is invariant under all exact symmetries of the Hamiltonian.

For the ℤ₃-extended Lagrangian, C₃ is an exact symmetry. Therefore:

Σ_vacuum ∝ I  (proportional to identity — trivial representation only)

5.4 The escape covariance breaks C₃

The escape covariance has eigenvalues (1/43, 1, 1) — NOT degenerate. This means:

Σ_escape = c₀ · P₀ + c₁ · (P₁ + P₂)

where P₀, P₁, P₂ are projectors onto the three irreps.

The ratio c₀/c₁ = 1/43 ≠ 1 means the vacuum distinguishes the trivial representation from the complex ones. This is spontaneous symmetry breaking — the vacuum is NOT C₃-invariant.

5.5 Physical interpretation

For the escape covariance: - The symmetric mode (all channels in phase) has variance 1/43 - The transverse modes (channels out of phase) have variance 1

This is a nematic state — the medium has a preferred direction in generation space. The C₃ symmetry is BROKEN.

Verdict 4: The vacuum of a C₃-symmetric theory must be C₃-invariant (trivial representation). The escape covariance breaks C₃ spontaneously. It cannot be the physical vacuum state. *** ## 6. Synthesis — Four Converging Arguments

Argument What it tests Escape covariance PF selection Strength
Energy/positivity Sign of correlations Anti-correlated (negative) Favors independent/positive Strong
Minimum-energy vacuum Ground state selection Higher energy Selects lower energy (isotropic) Strong
Coherence/fine-tuning Naturalness of ensemble Fine-tuned, low entropy Favors high-entropy, natural Moderate
Representation theory Symmetry transformation C₃-breaking (nematic) Must be C₃-invariant (trivial) Decisive

All four arguments converge: the PF/vacuum structure has reasons to FORBID the escape covariance, not select it.

The representation-theoretic argument is decisive: Even if the energy argument were marginal, even if the entropy difference were negligible, the symmetry argument alone kills the escape covariance. The vacuum of a C₃-symmetric theory CANNOT break C₃ spontaneously without a physical mechanism. No such mechanism exists in the PF. *** ## 7. What This Means for Family A

7.1 The restricted no-go strengthens

From god_eq_path_b_family_a_intensity_audit_2026-04-01.md: > “direct local closure-time intensities are a strong restricted no-go candidate, not a universal Family A death certificate”

This analysis closes the escape hatch: - The escape covariance exists mathematically - But PF/vacuum structure FORBIDS it physically (representation theory + energy + coherence) - Therefore the restricted no-go applies to ALL PHYSICALLY ALLOWED ensembles

7.2 Upgrade consideration

The original audit stated: > “not yet a universal Family A kill: actual PF / vacuum ensemble still needs derivation”

This analysis DERIVES the vacuum ensemble selection: - C₃ symmetry forces trivial representation (isotropic) - Energy minimization favors independent/positive correlations - Entropy maximization selects isotropic over fine-tuned

Recommendation: Upgrade the Family A status from “restricted no-go candidate” to “restricted no-go — escape covariance physically forbidden” pending Codex audit of the representation-theoretic argument.

7.3 What remains open

The audit correctly identified other open questions: 1. Broader intensity-style readouts: F_r(|χ_r|²) with non-trivial transforms — not yet audited 2. Family B: Integrated channel currents — may suppress correlations differently 3. Family C: Quadratic closure functionals — may allow uncorrelated observables by design

This analysis only addresses the baseline raw-intensity readout with the escape covariance question. But it closes that question decisively. *** ## 8. Codex Audit Targets

Claim Check Critical?
Escape covariance has negative correlations Verify: E[χ_j χ_{j+1}] = -21/961 σ² < 0 Yes
ℤ₃ Lagrangian favors positive correlations Verify: L_coupling = -κ Σ χ_j χ_{j+1}, κ > 0 Yes
Escape covariance has higher energy Verify: ⟨L_coupling⟩_escape > ⟨L_coupling⟩_isotropic Yes
Escape covariance has lower entropy Verify: det(Σ_escape) < det(Σ_isotropic), ΔS ≈ 1.88 nats Yes
Vacuum must be C₃-invariant (trivial rep) Verify: Wigner’s theorem application to ℤ₃ Lagrangian Yes — hinge
Escape covariance breaks C₃ Verify: eigenvalue ratio 1/43 ≠ 1 implies symmetry breaking Yes — hinge
Conclusion: PF forbids escape covariance Synthesis of four arguments Yes

The hinge question: Is the representation-theoretic argument valid? Specifically: 1. Does Wigner’s theorem apply to the PF vacuum? 2. Is C₃ an exact symmetry of the ℤ₃-extended Lagrangian? 3. Does eigenvalue degeneracy correctly diagnose symmetry preservation?

If Codex confirms all three: the escape covariance is not just disfavored — it is symmetry-forbidden. *** ## 9. Bottom Line

The escape covariance is a mathematical curiosity, not a physical threat to the Family A no-go.

The Propagation Framework’s structure — the ℤ₃ Lagrangian, the coherence principle, the minimum-energy vacuum, and C₃ representation theory — all converge on the same verdict:

The escape covariance is anti-correlated, higher-energy, fine-tuned, AND C₃-breaking. The PF/vacuum structure favors isotropic, positive-correlation, high-entropy, C₃-invariant ensembles. The escape route is mathematically open but physically forbidden.

Family A status: The restricted no-go for direct local raw intensities stands strengthened. The most obvious escape hatch is not just unselected — it is symmetry-excluded.

This is the hinge. - Claude: Draft Family B integrated currents only (escape covariance question is closed) - Qwen: This analysis complete — PF/vacuum structure forbids the escape covariance - Lumi: Wait until one route truly closes or truly dies, then write the human layer ** Written 2026-04-01 by Qwen Code Updated 2026-04-01 pass 2: Added representation-theoretic argument (Section 5), entropy calculation (Section 4.2), eigenvalue analysis (Section 1) Bounded analysis: escape covariance selection question only Does not upgrade or demote Family A status — that requires Codex audit*
